extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers, meta-researchers, and practitioners building automated systems to analyze peer reviews and estimate review quality
extracted.subtask_description: Annotation schema and dataset for sentence-level analysis of peer review texts (ICLR 2018) to support tasks like section correspondence, aspect detection, statement role/significance prediction and meta-review generation. Designed for NLP/ML work on peer-review quality and related meta-science research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1: Review–Paper Section Correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the section of the paper that a review statement is commenting on (annotated at sentence/segment level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels are simple and obvious for ML papers (see Table 2). Annotators should select the section (e.g., Methodology, Experiments, Results, Analysis, Abstract, Introduction, Future Work, Related Work, Overall paper, Problem Definition/Idea, Datasets, Tables/Figures, Bibliography, External Information). Some labels are inter-linked and hard to distinguish (e.g., Methodology vs Experiments vs Results vs Analysis). Use multi-labeling when multiple sections are involved and consider surrounding sentence context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Abstract (ABS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review statements that comment on the paper's abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rare; occur only when reviewers explicitly discuss the abstract. Consider overlapping with Introduction/Overall if ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Introduction (INT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review statements that address the introduction, presentation of problem and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often used to mark summaries and initial reviewer understanding; annotators noted overlap between INT and OAL (overall/abstract).

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Overall/General (OAL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments about the overall paper or generic comments not tied to a single section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can appear anywhere in the review (beginning, middle, end). When in doubt between OAL and INT, consider combined interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Problem Definition / Idea (PDI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements addressing the problem formulation, idea, or novelty of the paper's central contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when reviewers discuss whether the core idea is well-defined or interesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Methodology (MET)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments addressing methods, model design, algorithms, or theoretical approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the most frequent labels; Methodology and Experiments/Results/Analysis are tightly linked and may require careful distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Experiments (EXP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments about experimental design, datasets, hyperparameters, runtimes, or empirical evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators should separate EXP from Results (RES) and Analysis (ANA) when possible; often co-occurs with empirical aspect labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Results (RES)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements about observed results, reported metrics, and empirical findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish from EXP (design) and ANA (interpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Analysis (ANA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that analyze results, interpret experiments, or provide insight into findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close to Results but focused on interpretation; can be subtle to separate from RES.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Related Work / Literature (RWK)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments concerning literature review, comparisons to prior work, or adequacy of citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cases where reviewers note missing comparisons or prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments addressing datasets used, dataset quality, appropriateness, or availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant for empirical evaluations and reproducibility concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Tables / Figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements about presentation or content of tables and figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor but present in some reviews; may involve formatting or axis suggestions (e.g., same axis limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments about references, citation completeness, or bibliographic errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often rare but present when literature coverage is criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — Future Work (FWK)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions or comments about extensions or future directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasionally invoked when reviewer suggests next steps or notes missing directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 1 label — External Information (EXT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments that bring in external background information or comparisons not in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when reviewer references external sources, community discussion, or contextual facts beyond the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2: Review–Paper Aspect Category
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which aspect of the paper the review statement addresses (e.g., novelty, empirical/theoretical soundness, clarity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspect-labels are intuitive for empirical ML (see Table 2). If a sentence does not conform to any prescribed aspect, leave unlabeled. Record sentiment (POS/NEG/NEU) for each aspect label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect — Empirical / Theoretical Soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments about the correctness, rigor, and soundness of experiments or theoretical claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the primary aspects reviewers focus on; high prevalence in ML reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect — Meaningful Comparisons (CMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments regarding whether comparisons to prior work are appropriate, fair, and meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes demands for baseline comparisons, ablation studies, or fairness in experimental setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect — Substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments about the volume, substance, or depth of the contribution (e.g., completeness of work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers whether the paper contains enough material to warrant acceptance or further work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect — Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments about clarity of exposition, writing, and understandability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes suggestions to improve explanation, notation, or organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect — Presentation and Formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on formatting, presentation quality, figure/table clarity, and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often actionable minor comments; overlaps with Tables/Figures label in Layer 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect — Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments assessing the potential impact or significance of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when reviewers discuss broader relevance or likely influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect — Novelty / Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on the novelty, originality, or newness of the ideas or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often implicit rather than explicit in reviews; reviewers may question novelty or cite prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect — Recommendation / Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments tied to suitability for venue, scope appropriateness, or explicit recommendation signals in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers often use the recommendation score field rather than text; explicit recommendation comments in text are less frequent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 2 sentiment labeling (POS/NEG/NEU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record reviewer sentiment (positive, negative, neutral) associated with each label in Layer 1 and Layer 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentiment is a useful signal of reviewer perspective toward particular sections/aspects; annotate polarity per label occurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 3: Review-statement Purpose / Role
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the purpose or role of each review statement (what the reviewer is doing in that sentence—summary, criticism, suggestion, question, appreciation, discussion, recommendation, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-label allowed because some statements serve multiple roles (e.g., deficit + suggestion). Table 3 lists label descriptions and examples. Purpose labels help infer reviewer intent and contribute to review quality signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — Summary (SMY)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements that present a concise summary of the work to indicate reviewer understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often at the start of reviews; marks the reviewer's description of the paper's contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — Criticism (CRT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements that criticize aspects of the work or highlight shortcomings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May overlap with Deficit; in constructive reviews criticism can be accompanied by suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — Deficit (DFT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements explicitly pointing out missing components, weaknesses, or deficits in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often appears in rejected-paper reviews more frequently than accepted ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — Suggestion / Suggestive Feedback (SUG / FBK)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements offering concrete suggestions or advice for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for constructive review; more common in accepted-paper reviews (as per dataset statistics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — Appreciation (APC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive evaluative statements praising the work or particular components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correlation: appreciation statements occur more in accepted-paper reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — Discussion / Insight (DIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer brings their understanding, knowledge, or broader discussion into the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often neutral in polarity and can include contextual knowledge or comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — Question (QSN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer poses clarifying questions or asks for clarifications from the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About 10% of comments are questions in this dataset; questions can point to deficits or request clarifications during rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — Recommendation / Feedback on Decision (REC/FBK)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements where the reviewer explicitly conveys their recommendation or takes a stand on paper fate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less frequent because reviewers often use dedicated recommendation score fields; when present, useful for meta-review drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer 4: Review-statement Significance (MAJ / MIN / GEN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the relative importance of each review statement within the review: Major comment (MAJ), Minor comment (MIN), General comment (GEN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: help editors/area chairs identify crucial statements that should influence decisions and meta-reviews. Major and minor comments are roughly equally present on average; general comments less frequent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance — Major Comment (MAJ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments judged to be crucial and influential to the review decision (substantive issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area chairs and authors would likely act on major comments; these can form part of the meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance — Minor Comment (MIN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Less-critical, often editorial or small methodological/experimental details that do not change the decision alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actionable but lower priority than MAJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance — General Comment (GEN)
rubrics_metrics.description: General discussion or commentary that is neither major nor minor in importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less likely to affect the decision; more contextual or opinionated remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustiveness as a review-quality dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which a review covers major sections and aspects of the paper (coverage breadth and depth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhaustiveness is an important dimension toward ascertaining review quality; review length is a signal but trivial baseline—coverage across sections/aspects, roles, and significant comments better indicate exhaustiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation unit and segmentation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotators should perform sentence-wise annotation but may select a text-segment; multi-label and phrase-level annotations allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sentence context when isolated sentences are ambiguous. Use phrase-level annotation if a sentence contains multiple aspects/sections with differing sentiment. Put confusing instances into a CANNOT DECIDE category for adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-label annotation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow multiple labels per segment when it addresses multiple sections, aspects, or serves multiple purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This handles overlaps (e.g., deficit + suggestion). The team may later merge related labels to reduce ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: CANNOT DECIDE / ambiguous-instance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When annotators cannot reliably assign labels, mark instance as CANNOT DECIDE for adjudication by the primary investigating team; ambiguous instances may be left out of final annotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to maintain annotation quality and inter-annotator agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record sentiment for Layer 1 and Layer 2 labels
rubrics_metrics.description: For each Layer 1 and Layer 2 label occurrence, also annotate sentiment (positive, negative, neutral).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentiment helps infer reviewer perspective and can be combined with other signals (roles, significance) to predict paper fate or review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing guidelines for experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard text preprocessing applied for baseline experiments: stop-word removal, stemming, removing irrelevant characters, lowercasing, and lemmatization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These preprocessing choices were used for reported baselines; downstream systems may choose different pipelines (e.g., preserve casing for neural models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream tasks / benchmark tasks defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Five NLP tasks supported by the dataset: Review Paper Section Correspondence, Paper Aspect Category Detection, Review Statement Role Prediction, Review Statement Significance Detection, and Meta-Review Generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tasks operationalize aspects of review quality (coverage, roles, importance) and enable building automated tools to assist editors, meta-reviewers, or author-facing feedback systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ICLR OpenReview data and sampling strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset collected from ICLR 2018 official reviews across accepted, rejected, and withdrawn papers to ensure diversity; stored per-review with standardized filenames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of ACC, REJ, WDR papers helps balance label distribution; reviewers' recommendation scores and final decisions were preserved as metadata for experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical/analysis criteria (label distribution and co-occurrence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze label distributions across accepted/rejected classes and co-occurrence between layers to understand how section labels map to aspect labels and how purposes/significance distribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use co-occurrence matrices to interpret which sections receive which aspects most often and to design models that leverage inter-layer dependencies.
